judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Indicators (rank 1, same Grade and Strand 'Geometry and Measurement'), so no different-rank direction is available and there is no substantive same-rank developmental evidence. B5.3.1.1.3 (Sub-Strand 1: Lines and Shapes) has learners prove a polygon is regular by measuring sides and angles or by folding/superimposing; B5.3.2.1.2 (Sub-Strand 2: Measurement, under B5.3.2.1 estimating/measuring perimeter and surface area of 2-D shapes in cm and m) has learners calculate perimeter of given shapes in centimetres and metres. They share genuine skill coherence — measuring the side lengths of 2-D polygons and reasoning about equal sides — which makes them mutually reinforcing complementary skills (regularity supports side-length reasoning for perimeter; perimeter work practises side measurement), but neither statement's proficiency is evidenced as supporting success in the other, and the token/trigram and code-prefix nominations are weak (shared tokens limited to 'and' and shared segments 'b5','3') and cannot alone establish dependency. Evidence is limited by truncated source evidence for both endpoints and by upstream audit/merge context, including a merged Measurement Sub-Strand anomaly and a merged BASIC 5 Grade organizer, but the statement texts themselves are trustworthy enough to support a symmetric judgment.

First (B5.3.2.1.3) calculates surface area of given shapes in centimetres and metres; second (B5.3.2.1.2) calculates perimeter of given shapes in the same units; their LCs differ only in the 'surface area' vs 'perimeter' tag. judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 6 Indicators (rank 2, same grade) under Content Standard B6.1.1.1 ('quantities and place value for multi-digit numerals'), Sub-Strand 'Counting, Representation, Cardinality & Ordinality'. B6.1.1.1.2 (read and write numbers in figures and words up to 1,000,000,000; LCs 'read numbers in figures and in words', 'write numbers in figures and in words') establishes fluent naming and notation of multi-digit numerals by place-value units. B6.1.1.1.5 (round off/up/down whole numbers up to 100,000 to the nearest ten thousands, thousands, hundreds and tens; LCs tagged 'place value', 'rounding') requires learners to locate and name those specific place-value positions and decide the direction of adjustment, which is a substantively more demanding operation on the same numerals. Proficiency in reading/writing the numerals therefore supports success in rounding them, giving a same-rank developmental direction from the second SFI to the first rather than mere shared wording ('numbers', 'up to', '000') or a shared code prefix. Both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context and truncated source evidence, so this is an inferred curriculum-grounded judgment on bounded excerpts.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicators in Strand 1: Number, judged at the same statement-type grain. B5.1.3.1.2 (BASIC 5, rank 1) is 'Compare and order fractions' under the content standard on strategies for comparing fractions; B6.1.4.1.2 (BASIC 6, rank 2) is 'Express ratios in equivalent forms, compare and order ratios' under B6.1.4.1, which explicitly frames ratios in terms of their relationship to fractions. The LCs ('Compare fractions'/'Order fractions' vs 'Compare ratios'/'Order ratios'/'Express ratios in equivalent forms') show the same comparison-and-ordering reasoning extended from fractions to ratios, with the added demand of equivalent-form generation. Proficiency in comparing and ordering fractions (equivalence, common denominators) plausibly supports success with comparing and ordering ratios at the higher grade, so lower-to-higher buildsTowards is supported rather than mere lexical 'compare/order' overlap.

judgment.rationale: Both Indicators sit under the same BASIC 4 Content Standard B4.3.3.2 ('Demonstrate an understanding of area of regular and irregular 2-D shapes'), Sub-Strand 'Measurement- (Perimeter and Area)', so the grain and topic match. B4.3.3.2.1 (second) requires recognising that area is measured in square units (LC: 'Recognise that area is measured in square units'), while B4.3.3.2.4 (first) requires developing and applying a formula for the area of a rectangle and square (LCs: 'Develop...' and 'Apply a formula for determining the area of a rectangle and square'). Although both carry canonical rank 0 (BASIC 4), the substantive change is from conceptual recognition of the square-unit basis of area measurement to deriving and using a multiplicative formula that presupposes that unit concept; proficiency with square-unit area measurement supports success in developing/applying the rectangle and square area formula, giving a directional second_to_first reading rather than mere symmetric reinforcement. Source page proximity, code prefix, and shared 'area/square' tokens were treated only as nomination signals, not as verdict evidence. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), so the excerpted exemplars are partial; the statement texts and LCs themselves are unambiguous enough to support this judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 6 Content Standards in Strand 2: Algebra (same statement-type grain, same rank 2), but in different sub-strands: B6.2.2.1 'Demonstrate understanding of algebraic expressions' (Sub-Strand 2: Algebraic Expressions) and B6.2.3.1 'Solve problems involving single-variable, one-step equations with whole number coefficients' (Sub-Strand 3: Variables and Equations). Substantively, facility with algebraic expressions as phrases containing letters standing for numbers (source excerpt shows writing expressions for areas) is the representational foundation for forming and manipulating a single-variable one-step equation and solving problems with it; proficiency in the expressions standard supports success in the equation-solving standard, giving a same-rank developmental direction from second to first rather than mere shared-parent or code-prefix proximity. Evidence limits: nomination rested partly on weak signals (code prefix, page proximity, trivial trigram overlap), no Learning Components were supplied for either endpoint, and both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 and 26 omitted items), so the judgment relies on the full statement texts and sub-strand placement available here.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 5 Indicators (rank 1, same Grade coordinate) under the same Content Standard B5.1.1.1 (place value/quantities) and Sub-Strand 'Counting, Representation & Cardinality'. B5.1.1.1.6 is skip counting forwards and backwards in 500s/1000s up to and from 100,000; B5.1.1.1.4 is comparing and ordering whole numbers up to 100,000 with >, <, =. They share the same number range and coherent number-sense content (sequencing/positioning versus relational comparison and symbolic representation), so they meaningfully reinforce one another as complementary skills. The evidence shows no substantive same-rank developmental dependency: skip counting is not presented as required for comparison/ordering, nor the reverse, and local code order (.4 before .6) is source sequence, not asserted progression. Symmetric relatesTo therefore fits; upstream merge/audit context on the shared Content Standard (stale 'CONT'D' continuation pattern) and truncated source evidence for both endpoints limit deeper inference but do not affect the shared topical grain.
